overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: a budget discussion with only two of five members present was not a deliberation, so no meeting occurred. The February 22 allegations were untimely, and the rule of necessity claim is outside the law's scope.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board held an improper April 11 meeting when it proceeded with only two of its five members present, short of a quorum.
allegations.key_passage: Because only two members participated in that portion of the discussion, the Board did not deliberate and thus did not hold a "meeting" for the purposes of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a second meeting on February 22 proceeded with less than a quorum; the complaint was filed more than 30 days after that meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the complaint was filed more than 30 days after the February 22 meeting occurred and the alleged violation took place in an open meeting, and thus could have been known at the time it occurred, the allegations concerning that meeting are untimely and we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board improperly invoked the 'rule of necessity' at its April 11 meeting to proceed with less than a quorum.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not address the rule of necessity, and thus we decline to review allegations of improper invocation of the rule.
